republican-jubilee-frankfort-1880-11-03.A3: POLITICAL SHOOTING IN KENTUCKY.—During a republican jollification at Frankfort, Ky., Wednesday night a difficulty occurred between Hon. W. H. Sneed and Jesse Lee. Lee drew a pistol, when Officer Conway interfered, and Lee's pistol went off in his hands, the ball taking effect in the lower part of Conway's bowels, inflicting what is thought will be a fatal wound. In a few minutes after a young white man named Frank Egbert, shot a negro boy named George Whittaker, who was cheering for Garnfield, the ball taking effect in the left side, just below the heart. It is thought he will not recover, though he is somewhat easier.

-The Congressional delegation from Virginia stands seven Democrats and two Republicans, a loss of one. Bailey, the Republican candidate in the 8th District, will contest Mr. John S. Barbour's seat on the grounds that voters were bulldozed, and that Mr. Barbour does not live in the District, but makes his home in Washington. Mr. Barbour has, however, always retained his voting place in Alexandria.

-Gen. Sheridan's annual report to the General of the Army sets forth that there are in the Department of Dakota 4,850 officers and men; in the Department of the Platte, 2,840; in the Department of Missouri, 4,720, and in the Department of Texas, 4,650. He considers this force entirely inadequate to the great territory and numerous demands upon the army from the Northern and Southern borders.

-The present Congress will have the right to apportion the representation for members of the House under the late census provided the census is completed in due season. It has been customary, however, for the apportionment to be made by the Congress that meets in the year next after the census was taken, which, in the pending case would be the Congress that will assemble in December, 1881.

—William Judd, mail contractor from Columbia to Burksville, was found dead in a tobacco barn near his residence, one mile west of Columbia. An inquest was held, and the verdict was death from strangulation by his own hand. The means used was a silk handkerchief tied around his neck and a stick run through to tighten until it produced the result stated. No cause stated why he took his own life.

—Thompson Conway, of Frankfort, the police officer who was shot by Capt. Jerry Lee while interfering in a difficulty between Capt. Lee and Judge Sneed, on Wednesday night, died from the effects of the wound. He made a dying statement that the shooting was accidental. He leaves a wife and five children to mourn his loss. Capt. Lee bore the expenses of the funeral and has since deeded the most of his property to the widow.

It is rumored here to-day that the Democratic leaders of the South will hold a meeting in Richmond shortly to consider the advisability of instructing all the Democratic Presidential electors of the South to cast their electoral votes for Garfield and make his election unanimous. Several leading Southern men stopping here express themselves as thoroughly disgusted with the Northern Democracy, and say that the South now has it in her power to break up the party whose Northern managers have so often betrayed them. Wade Hampton is said to be of this opinion, and strongly in favor of making Garfield's election unanimous. [Washington Dispatch.

It is estimated that by the next apportionment of representation in Congress New England will lose four, the Middle States six, the South gain three and the West gain seven. By the new ratio there will be one Representative to one hundred and seventy thousand inhabitants. Ohio will have nineteen Representatives a loss of one.
Two Louisville boys after reading numerous dime novels which told of the wonderful exploits of fast boys and men, determined to go South. They did not have money enough to pay the railroad fare for both so one of them agreed to go in a trunk and be shipped as the other's baggage. Several holes were bored in the side of the trunk to give him air and everything went all right till passing Bowling Green when the Baggage Master began to pile the trunks up. This shut off the air and the boy hallooed to be let out. The B. republican-jubilee-frankfort-1880-11-03.A6:
MISCELLANEOUS
Gov. Roberts has revoked the Texas quarantine, to take place Wednesday.

There is a complaint of scarcity of silver money in Montgomery, Ala.

The Democrats at Uniontown cut down their flag-pole before the election returns were all in.

The Outlook says there was not a dollar of money used in Bath county by either of the political parties.

Hon. Jos. M. Davidson, who has been seriously ill for a month or more, has recovered.

Stanford has a new hall, and a Cincinnati man has been employed to paint a drop curtain and six scenes.

Judge Phister's majority is over one thousand. It was reported last week at two hundred.

J. C. S. Blackburn and James A. Garfield received the same number of votes in Fayette county.

Thomas B. Ford has been re-elected as Common School Commissioner for Franklin county.

The Memphis Appeal says that the South is prosperous only on account of the industry and frugality of her people.

The public schools of Americus, Ga., are attended by an equal number of white and colored students.

In Nicholas county, W. Va., James Austin, aged thirteen, and George Mastin, aged sixteen, killed during a week's hunt four deer.

The Owingsville Outlook and Winchester Sun are offering premiums for the best specimens of tobacco grown in their respective counties.

Burton Holland killed himself by hanging in Pulaski county. Financial misfortune is supposed to have been the cause.

The editor of the Logan County News reminds his subscribers that he is housekeeping, and will exchange subscriptions for farm products.

The 4 p. m. train on the K. C. R. R. going North does not put off, but takes on mail between Lexington and Cincinnati.

A large number of negroes at Dawson, Ga., went to the next town to a circus in preference to staying at home and voting.

Yazoo county, Miss., has appropriated a large sum of money for the purpose of having all the public roads surveyed, repaired and mile posts erected.

Last Thursday night a party of burglars went through a whole block of stores in Louisville, and only obtained $35. To get money now-a-days, by such means, one must go to a bank.

The Covington Commonwealth says that some of the Democrats in the Legislature by their actions last winter helped to elect John D. White to Congress.

The Frankfort Yeoman during the whole administration of Rutherford B. Hayes has never honored that individual by speaking of him as the President of the United States.

A sale of $20,000 in Tennessee bonds was made in Nashville at forty-six cents on the dollar, a heavy advance on the rates which have ruled for some time past.

Prof. Robert Harris, colored, the principal of the State Normal School at Fayetteville, N. C., for educating colored teachers, died in that town the other day.

William A. Roberts, of Union county, recently sold his hay crop for the last three years, amounting to 350 tons, and will be prepared to make one shipment of 7,000 bales.

Young Egbert, who shot the negro boy Whittaker, at Frankfort, on the 3d inst., has given himself into the custody of the officers. His examining trial closed yesterday, when he was held over to the Circuit Court in $500 bond.

The Owingsville Outlook will not be held responsible for the recent Democratic disappointment. It was for Tilden in '76, and if he is forgiving enough to look over a party's gross ingratitude, will be for him in '84, if alive, and for his corpse, if dead.

Mrs. Phoebe Bailey, who lives in Halifax county, Va., was robbed a few nights ago of $600 in money and $7,000 in bonds. The thief, named Dave Bailey, was admitted to the house by the servant girl. The bonds were burned by the thieves—both of whom are in jail.

There will be five negro men in the Tennessee Legislature, three from Shelby, one from Tipton, and one from Davidson county. T. A. Sykes, the negro member from Davidson, was one time a member of the North Carolina Legislature.

Burwell Whaley and Miss Maggie Bell eloped from Grant county and were married at Falmouth. The young lady being under legal age, County Judge Perrin held open court and appointed the groom her guardian.

Polk Prince, of Todd county, has sixty Angora goats on his farm, and says the rearing of them is much more profitable than the cultivation of tobacco. The average yield of wool from these goats is five pounds, and it is worth seventy-five cents per pound.

The Yeoman says the examining trial of Frank Egbert for shooting George Whitaker took place before Judge Thomson on Tuesday morning, and he was held to bail for his appearance at the next term of Circuit Court in the sum of $500 which he gave.

is sold in Hopkinsville by sample to competitive buyers representing all wheat buying sections. Sacks are furnished to the farmers by the buyers, and he fills them and delivers the grain in his wagon and is paid for it on delivery, thus saving all storage and commission.

It is expected that the Mardi Gras festivities at New Orleans will attract a larger number of visitors this winter than ever before. A number of excursions will be organized in Texas in sections which have not been accessible herefore. The crack Seventy-first regiment, of New York City, will visit New Orleans during the carnival, and will be the guests of the Washington artillery.

In digging a place for a foundation to a new building in Columbus, Texas, the workmen found at the depth of only ten inches below the surface a skull and bones of a man. The skull being thin is considered evidence that it belonged to a white man. Old citizens have put their heads together endeavoring to remember some mystery in the past history of Columbus.

The New Orleans Picayune has some statistics showing that before the civil war the South had more taxable property on her rolls than New England and the Middle States combined. After the contest and five years of peace, she had
on her Toll than New England and the Middle States combined. After the contest and five years of peace, she had bunk $300,000,000 below the New England States alone. In 1860 forty per cent. of all the real and personal property assessed in the United States was in the Southern States, while now they have only fourteen per cent.

Last Monday morning, while Mr. Steve Robinson was in his room he received an epileptic stroke and fell in the fire and was severely burned. His back was almost charred. He probably would have been burned to death had it not been for a boy, who was catching his horse, preparatory to his going to Lexington, come into the room to tell him his horse was ready, just in time to save his life. He is doing very well now, and will recover. Fortunately, his face will not be disfigured.
